QuestionStmt.S: $$f(x) = (\cos x + i \sin x) \cdot (\cos 3x + i \sin 3x) \cdots [\cos(2n-1)x + i \sin(2n-1)x]$$ Then $f''(x) =$ (where $i = \sqrt{-1}$)

Solution.S:
Using Euler's formula, $\cos kx + i \sin kx = e^{ikx}$. Thus:
$$f(x) = e^{ix} \cdot e^{i3x} \cdots e^{i(2n-1)x} = e^{i[x + 3x + 5x + \cdots + (2n-1)x]}.$$

The sum of the first $n$ odd numbers is $n^2$, so the exponent becomes $i n^2 x$. Hence:
$$f(x) = e^{i n^2 x}.$$

First derivative: $f'(x) = i n^2 e^{i n^2 x} = i n^2 f(x)$.

Second derivative: $f''(x) = (i n^2)^2 e^{i n^2 x} = i^2 n^4 f(x) = -n^4 f(x)$.

Therefore $f''(x) = -n^4 f(x)$, which matches option B.
